newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish pound recovers after sharp fall.
newsitem.headline: Irish pound recovers after sharp fall.

text.p: The Irish pound clawed back some ground in early trade on Friday, after plunging by more than three pfennigs against the mark and losing a penny against sterling in late trade on Thursday, dealers said.

They said the sharp fall was triggered by a larger sell order out of the U.S., which caught the market long and caused the punt to nosedive from 0.8820 to 0.8730 stg, while dropping from over 2.71 marks back below 2.6800.
Dealers said the move may have reflected fading hopes of a revaluation and further weakness could be in store.
"The first move in the Irish pound is often only the beginning. I wouldn't be surprised to see it go weaker again today," one trader said.
By 0730 GMT, the Irish pound was at 0.8785 sterling and 2.6825 marks against 0.8730 and 2.6775 late yesterday.
Pressure on the punt at the top of the ERM grid eased. It was trading 11.65 percent above the French franc compared with a gap of more than 12 percent recently.
The punt was helped this morning by a sharp drop in sterling as cable crashed after breaking below $1.6670, dragging sterling/mark down by more than 1.5 pfennigs.
But dealers said people were getting bored with the revaluation play which has helped support the Irish pound against the mark in recent weeks and the punt could have further to fall.
"The market has been waiting for it to happen for the guts of a month now and it doesn't appear to be any closer, so maybe people are beginning to look at the whole situation again," one dealer said.

Traders also said recent developments on EMU, which point increasingly toward a widely-based weak euro, meant the market might now be starting to turn its attention back to what levels currencies are likely to enter EMU at.

The Irish pound was trading well above its central ERM parity of 2.41 marks, the cause of heavy selling in April as the market believes it would have to fall back toward those levels before EMU in the absence of a revaluation.
"The convergence play on the punt may come back into vogue again," the dealer said.
